The bounded schedule contains four blocks of eight sweeps: (step radians, shots/group) = (0.4, 256), (0.2, 512), (0.1, 1024), (0.05, 2048). The initial objective uses 256 shots/group. Each sweep freshly measures its incumbent and both coordinate proposals for every parameter, including all rejected proposals. A candidate is accepted only when the sampled decrease exceeds twice the combined estimated standard error; this margin is a heuristic, without a confidence or convergence guarantee across adaptive choices. Every run stops after the prescribed 32 sweeps.

Each seed is paired with a different fixed initialization. These six cases jointly vary initialization and measurement randomness; they do not isolate the two effects. Fresh validation uses 4,096 shots per group and a separate keyed random-stream family after training ends.

Fresh validation estimates the energy or expected cut of the final, already selected state. The estimated standard error includes within-group covariance; it is not a rigorous interval. The separate Hoeffding radius is an ideal-sampling 95% bound for each validation row, not simultaneous table coverage.

The post-run numerical targets are exact expected cut at least 2.90 for QAOA and exact energy gap at most 0.03 for VQE. These diagnostics assess the selected toy states after training; target flags are not guarantees derived from the validation confidence bound.

A fixed, fully recorded training schedule

children.label: A fixed, fully recorded training schedule

children.value: The sampled polling optimizer makes one initial objective call at 256 shots per group. It then runs 32 sweeps in four blocks. Each block uses its stated step and shot count for all eight sweeps; lack of an accepted move does not alter the schedule.

Every sweep remeasures the incumbent at that sweep’s shot count, then evaluates both negative and positive displacements along each coordinate from that same incumbent. QAOA therefore uses five objective calls per sweep: one incumbent and four proposals. VQE uses three: one incumbent and two proposals. Angles are reduced modulo

The combined standard error is descriptive: the rule is not a calibrated hypothesis test or a 95% acceptance guarantee. Selecting among proposals, repeating adaptive comparisons, and occasionally obtaining zero empirical variance prevent that interpretation. An accepted sampled improvement can be an exact deterioration, and a rejected move can be an exact improvement.

. Algorithm IDs are zero for QAOA and one for VQE; family zero is training and family one is fresh final validation. Keys distinguish calls and measurement groups. They support reproducibility and avoid accidental stream reuse; they do not mathematically prove independence of a pseudorandom generator. The statistical statements here use the ideal independent-sampling model.

retains every sampled call, candidate parameters, group counts, group means, standard errors, stream identifiers, accepted and rejected moves, stopping reason, classical optimizer time, and post-training diagnostics. No exact expectation or analytic derivative enters the acceptance rule.

The plotted exact cut or energy along a trajectory is a diagnostic, rather than an objective available to the sampled optimizer. The exact optimizer from the first increment remains an independent reference. Three predetermined trajectories show behavior on these instances; the fraction meeting a target is not a certified population success probability.

expectation estimate. Six individually 95% intervals do not provide a simultaneous 95% statement for all runs. The VQE formula already bounds the combined Z/X estimate; it does not need an additional group split for this statistical interval.

Fresh holdout coverage remains valid conditional on the training history and selected angles under the independent-sampling model. It bounds readout error at those angles. It does not prove that training achieved a target, bound the optimizer’s failure probability, or turn the observed mean into certified optimal angles. In particular, a holdout interval can be too wide to certify the requested
VQE energy gap even when the toy’s exact diagnostic meets it. Sampled energy can also fall below the exact ground energy through readout noise.

All proposals and all incumbent remeasurements count, including rejected moves and the initial call. With the default schedule, one QAOA run has 161 objective calls and 153,856 training shots. One VQE run has 97 objective calls, each with two groups, and 184,832 training shots. These totals follow from the executed trace, rather than from the number of accepted updates.
Workload for the three predetermined runs

Each shot represents a new state preparation in the ideal circuit protocol. The implementation draws counts classically from circuit probabilities, so these are protocol shot counts rather than physical circuit executions. The

weights the actual circuit gates by every call’s shot count, separates training from validation, includes basis changes and qubit readout, and records unsynthesized rotations. A single final ansatz evaluation is not this hybrid run.

CPU timings measure the local simulator, random sampling, and classical control. They do not measure a quantum device’s reset, routing, gate, measurement, communication, or feedback latency. Input parsing and separate classical reference timing are disclosed where unmeasured. The exact diagnostics and figure-generation work are additional classical checks rather than hidden quantum objective evaluations. The
accounts for this fixed training record; it does not predict a fresh hardware-driven adaptive execution.
Conditional resources for a fixed final readout

children.label: Conditional resources for a fixed final readout

children.value: The projection takes seed 7’s fitted final angles as fixed classical inputs. It estimates only 4,096 QAOA all-Z executions and, separately, 4,096 VQE all-Z plus 4,096 VQE all-X executions. It includes the explicit preparations, rotations, basis changes, and readout of those exported circuits. The sampled training decisions and their million-shot workload are excluded from this physical projection.

These two declared choices select each group’s point separately; they do not claim a full combined Pareto frontier. Serial group time is summed and peak physical qubits use the maximum, rather than adding independent peaks. This assumes reuse or reconfiguration between independent group layouts/factories; configuration-change and communication overhead are excluded, and a common joint hardware layout is not certified.

The separate ideal fixed-state 95% Hoeffding radii are 0.084881 for the mean cut and 0.087494 for energy. The VQE bound uses two independent bounded groups and preserves Z-term covariance. No certified confidence combining sampling, synthesis and physical faults is reported.
